svg.title: FDAI reference architecture
svg.desc: Connected Azure resources, telemetry, repositories, and enterprise connectors publish typed signals into the headless FDAI control plane. Operators use the Web Console, CLI, and ChatOps interfaces. Fifteen independently runnable agents own every control stage and coordinate through a schema-validated event bus. Events pass through ingest and trust routing into T0 deterministic rules, T1 verified reuse, or T2 grounded reasoning. T2 alone passes a mixed-model quality gate before all tiers enter the common risk and authority gate. High-impact work requests independent human authority, and the resulting typed approval event re-enters the agent runtime instead of calling the executor directly. Eligible work reaches the privileged executor and produces remediation pull requests or bounded direct actions; ineligible work is held, denied, or closed as a no-op. Microsoft Foundry, Azure OpenAI, provider tools, OPA and Rego policy evaluation, IQL inventory queries, the operating ontology, governed catalogs, and PostgreSQL provide governed capabilities outside the headless control-plane boundary. Azure Container Apps, Microsoft Entra ID, managed identities, Key Vault, and Azure Monitor form the deployment foundation. Every terminal result is attributable and replayable.
svg.text: Agent-owned control stages, separated authority gates, governed dependencies, and outcomes for FDAI autonomous cloud operations.

text.tspan: Governed provider, policy, knowledge, and evidence capabilities

g.aria-label: Azure deployment foundation
Typed event choreography and ownership
Agent-owned governed control flow
Azure resources. Subscription and resource inventory
Operational telemetry. Metrics, logs, traces, alerts, and changes
Source repositories. Infrastructure, application, policy, and catalog changes
Documents and connectors. Authenticated enterprise sources and governed uploads
FDAI Web Console. Read projections and submit bounded requests
FDAI CLI. Scriptable operator access through the Operator API
ChatOps. Teams, Slack, and notification adapters
Schema-validated event bus. Pub/sub, retry, isolation, dead-letter, and replay
15 agents own every stage. Single-writer ownership for observation, judgment, approval, execution, recovery, audit, and learning
Event ingest. Validate, normalize, deduplicate, and correlate
Trust router. Select the lowest competent tier
T0 / T1 / T2 decisions. T0 rules, T1 verified reuse, or T2 grounded reasoning
T2-only quality gate. Mixed-model agreement, grounding, and deterministic verification
Risk and authority gate. Policy, ActionType ceiling, impact scope, approval, and safeguards
Privileged executor. Bounded action with lock and rollback
Microsoft Foundry. Model, evaluation, and agent project plane
Azure OpenAI. Optional governed T2 capabilities
Provider tools and MCP. Registered read and action adapters behind typed contracts
OPA / Rego + IQL. Deterministic policy evaluation and bounded inventory queries
Ontology and catalogs. Objects, evidence, rules, ActionTypes, workflows, and promotion records
PostgreSQL and pgvector. State, append-only audit, evidence, and context
Container Apps. Runtime and scheduled jobs
Microsoft Entra ID. Human authentication and App Roles
Managed identities. Separated workload authority
Key Vault. Secret references and connection material
Azure Monitor. Traces, metrics, logs, and alerts
Held, denied, or no-op. No mutation when evidence, policy, or authority is insufficient
Governed changes. Remediation pull request or bounded direct action
Audit and replay. Attributable terminal evidence and deterministic reconstruction
Independent human authority. Current approval or valid bounded standing authorization
